Narcolepsy type 2 is a neurologic sleep-wake disorder. Its hallucinations and sleep symptoms do not establish damage to another organ axis.

Eye and esophageal malformations define the syndrome; frequent tracheoesophageal fistula supports pulmonary labeling. Callosal agenesis supports neurologic involvement; hearing impairment is reasonably omitted under the four-axis cap.
The oral-acral malformation phenotype supports gastrointestinal and musculoskeletal primary axes. Sparse evidence warrants low confidence; no additional organ involvement is established.
CLN2 disease is a lysosomal metabolic disorder defined by neurodegeneration. Progressive retinal degeneration and visual loss commonly occur over the typical late-infantile course.

Meningeal inflammation establishes neurologic disease. Noninfectious meningitis includes causes without autoimmune or other qualifying immune mechanisms, so infectious_immune is not required across this umbrella.

Neurodevelopmental abnormalities support neurologic primary labeling. Supplied HPO frequencies support damaging ocular and muscular involvement. Cancer predisposition does not justify labeling potential tumor organs or blood.

Canavan disease is a metabolic leukodystrophy. Optic atrophy at 80-99% and hearing impairment at 30-79% support ocular and otologic involvement; feeding difficulty alone does not establish gastrointestinal damage.

Choroidal atrophy and hair/nail abnormalities define ocular and dermatologic disease. This subtype has no established defining dental or oral abnormalities; occasional glue ear does not meet the involvement threshold.

Brain malformations and arthrogryposis define neurologic and musculoskeletal disease; pulmonary hypoplasia in 2/3 supports involvement. Fetal pyelectasis alone does not establish renal damage; broader PI4KA phenotypes need not apply.
